title: A small test set with expected answers

sections.skill: Build a small test set with expected answers

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: What is a test set?

choices.text: A collection of the tool's own past answers, saved so they can be shown to new users

questions.intro: Before trusting a tool for a recurring task, build a small TEST SET: 10 to 20 REAL examples of the task, each with an EXPECTED ANSWER you worked out or confirmed yourself. Include ordinary cases and a few hard or unusual ones. Run the tool on every example, compare with the expected answers, and count how many it gets right. Write down which ones it got wrong and how. Example: to judge a tool that sorts customer emails, collect 20 past emails whose correct category you know, then check its sorting against yours.

sections.skill: Compare a test set with a practice exam with an answer key

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: What does the answer key do?

choices.text: Lets you tell right from wrong

questions.correct_answer: Lets you tell right from wrong
questions.intro: A teacher deciding whether a new textbook's practice problems are accurate might work 15 problems herself, writing an ANSWER KEY, and then compare the textbook's answers with hers. A tool test set is the same: real tasks plus an answer key you trust. Without the key, you cannot tell right from wrong; with only easy problems, you learn little.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: A test set contains only easy examples. What happens?

choices.text: The tool looks worse than it really is, since easy examples confuse most AI tools
The tool looks better than it is

questions.correct_answer: The tool looks better than it is
questions.intro: Test sets go wrong in quiet ways. If you choose only easy examples, the tool looks better than it is. If your expected answers are wrong, you will blame the tool for your error. If you keep tweaking your request until it passes these 20 examples, it may fail on new ones, so keep a few examples aside for a final check. Rerun the same test set when the tool or your instructions change, and add new examples whenever a real failure surprises you.
